<!-- pr-reviewer: 025ed4760e592c3401859a66285457021a98341b -->

**Verdict: Not built - read-only review (outside contributor), no blockers found in the read. The PR also adds direct dependencies (Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock), so it waits for a maintainer look.**

@qsmits thank you for a very thorough PR. The read was complete; the build was not, so nothing below is a test result.

## What looks good

- Refusal-first design: `posting_agie.rs` and `operation/agie_profile.rs` refuse taper, four-axis, tabs, burnout, skims, fixtures, non-default options, per-op mode, multi-mount, non-mm units, smoothing, travel-declared X/Y and non-prism solids by name, before publication.
- Atomic publication: same-volume staging plus a NOREPLACE rename (`crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs:104-170`), with a clean error on unsupported platforms. The Windows arm checks for an embedded NUL and is cfg-split correctly.
- Numeric safety: `quantize` guards finiteness and range, `micrometres` uses `try_from` with a round-trip check, and the orientation math uses i128 (`crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs:13-23`). No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests in the new files.
- Layering holds: the writer is in `camcraft-post`, the document checks are in `camcraft-app`, the UI only calls the pure predicates. Components stay in `schema.rs` usage, none re-declared.
- License: the Agie Processor reference is your own MIT source, the notice is in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`, and the decision entry `docs/decisions/2945-native-agie-wire.md` names the dependencies and says why an external generator was dropped. No HSMWorks or Autodesk material appears in the new files.
- Goldens: `is_closed_convex_prism` in `crates/geometry` is a conservative all-facet check with its own pinning test; the CRLF byte rules in `.gitattributes` fit the controller format; the refusal records are explained in the body.

## Not built

- You are not a collaborator, so the PR test runner will not build this PR, and project rules keep reviewers from building outside code locally. No tests, no clippy, and no heavy lane ran for this review.
- "All 48 targeted checks passed" and the gate lines in the body are the author's readings, not verified here.
- This PR changes `crates/post/Cargo.toml`, `crates/app/Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (new direct deps: tempfile, rustix, windows-sys). Added dependencies are a "read, not built" item: a maintainer must look before any build.

## Conflicts

- GitHub reports this head as CONFLICTING. A local `git merge-tree` against current main (36348cda6) reported a clean merge, so GitHub may be stale or the criss-cross merge bases confuse its check. Please merge current `origin/main` into the branch once (not a rebase), so the state is unambiguous.

## Requested before merge

1. Merge current `origin/main` into the branch and push, as above.
2. Attach the updated Post dialog screenshots to the body. The body says the corrected picker and receipt readings were checked locally, but the body still shows the earlier writer's pictures only.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The body asks whether the Agie-CAM reference meets the source rules. The project's clean-room protocol protects HSMWorks and Autodesk material; your own MIT-published code with the notice retained is outside that rule. The maintainer makes the final call on the observed controller examples for the JEScript details.
- `queue_post_after_apply` picks a folder with a blocking dialog call on the UI thread (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/post_dialog.rs:283`). Other branches do the same, so this is not new; a note only.
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` is now 416 lines and `posting.rs` 1629 lines. Both files were already over the 400-line rule; this PR adds 2 and 17 lines. A split is owed in other work, not here.
- The X/Y travel refusal (`crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs:37-44`) blocks the native post for any operator who fills in the template's travel, even a large and safe one. The message explains it; a follow-up issue to verify travel against the margin could lift this later.
- The smoothing and dialog label changes add no UI structural test updates; the reviewer could not run the ui suites, so their state is unknown, not green.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Verdict: Not built - needs a maintainer look.** No blocker in the code itself.

## What looks good
- The native dispatcher validates everything before it writes: machine model and kind, one op, one mount, default post options, millimetre document, condition identity, prism shape, stock span and the entry lead. Each refusal names its cause.
- Publication is safe: staging in a sibling temp dir, `create_new` plus `sync_all` for each file, then a no-replace rename. An existing job directory cannot be touched (crates/post/src/agie/mod.rs).
- The new `geometry::is_closed_convex_prism` check examines every facet, so an internal cavity cannot pass an XY-only test. The test pins that case.
- The hand-resolved conflict in `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` is correct. I counted 21 shipped `.cps` files at this head: 20 text posts (one of them Klartext) plus the native Agie refusal. The remerge-diff shows that hunk is the only hand edit since `f92e67857`.
- Layering holds. New modules carry provenance lines. New files are under 400 lines. New test files carry Gate maps. No snapshot PNG and no existing golden changed; the goldens are add-only. The receipt sets `working_steps_generated=false` and keeps `lines` out.
- The dialog path queues `ApplyPostDialog` (a command); it does not write world state directly. The script and MCP surface reports the bundle files.

## Results
- Not built. This PR comes from a fork of an account without push access (qsmits). The self-hosted pr-test runner must not run fork code, and this machine could not build (disk at its limit). The review is read-only: the full diff against `5c8340b81` (v0.25.0), the merge head, and main.
- The contributor's checks are recorded in the body: 72 focused tests pass on this head, and clippy passes for app, geometry, post and ui. I did not run them.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches the post, app and ui heavy lanes (a geometry change reaches app). The body says the 259-step heavy gate was "running" at the head. A started run is not a result. A green heavy run at the final head is still owed (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Requested before merge
1. Decide the dependency change: `crates/post/Cargo.toml` adds `tempfile`, `rustix` and `windows-sys` as new direct (per-OS) dependencies, and `crates/app/Cargo.toml` adds `tempfile` as a dev-dependency. All three packages already exist in main's `Cargo.lock`, so no package enters the graph. A `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` change is "read, not built" and waits for the maintainer's build.
2. Decide the reference source. `docs/decisions/2945-native-agie-wire.md` states that some JEScript and QN2 details follow the contributor's own MIT Agie-CAM repo and observed controller examples. The MIT notice is already in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` on main. Agie is not Autodesk material, so the Clean-Room Protocol does not bar it; the Reference-material list is narrower than "observed controller examples". This is the open question on #2945; it needs your word.
3. Run one quick gate and the reached heavy lanes on the final head on a machine with build access before the ready flag.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The body names the machine template as #2948; the decision file names it #2946. `assets/machines/agiecut-classic-2s.mch` is already on main, so one of the two references is wrong in a text only.
- `crates/app/src/posting_agie.rs` refuses a profile with a stated X or Y travel. The asymmetry with the generic wire post is deliberate and the user guide explains it. I read it as sound.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` grows past 1,600 lines. Pre-existing; not caused here.
- Process: no process file is touched, so no `Process change:` line is needed. The commit subjects are conventional and the body ends with `Fixes #2945` with a `Changelog:` line. Both hold.
- The PR is a draft and a `feat`. It merges at a cut, per Pull Request Law, so the label keeps it visible without hurry.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
